**SSHIT-Commander** ist ein Dual-Pane-Da:
**SSHIT-Commander** is a dual-pane file manager with an integrated SSH/SFTP terminal.

- A **pane** on each side — local or remote, operated the same way.
- Below each pane a **console** with two modes: *Commands* and *Terminal*.
- Any number of **tabs**, each with its own connection.
- All network work runs on background threads — the window never freezes during SSH operations or transfers.
*Ansicht → Theme* schaltet zwischen **Du:
*View → Theme* switches between **Dark**, **Midnight**, **Light** and **High Contrast**; the choice is saved and also applies to the terminal.

*View → Theme editor* creates your own colour schemes: pick a base, click the colour swatches (background, surfaces, borders, text, accents, scrollbars, terminal colours) and save under your own name. The **preview** at the bottom shows the result immediately.

*View → Preview* shows a preview panel below each pane displaying the selected file read-only (text or image).
*Clipboard → Clipboard-Manager* führt ei:
*Clipboard → Clipboard manager* keeps a history of everything copied.

- Double-click sets an entry as the **active** clipboard content.
- *Insert* writes the entry into the active console.
- Individual entries or the whole list can be deleted.
*Tools → Datei-Alarm* überwacht Ordner a:
*Tools → File alarm* watches folders for changes.

- Per alarm: **name**, **folder**, watched **events** (created, modified, deleted), **include subfolders**, **count folders** and *active*.
- Watching runs in the background by snapshot comparison; events appear in the list and in the status bar.
*Tools → Datei-Encoding konvertieren* wa:
*Tools → Convert file encoding* converts text files between character sets — UTF-8/16/32, Windows-1250/1251/1252, ISO 8859-1/15, DOS/OEM 437/850, Mac Roman, KOI8-R, Shift-JIS, GBK, Big5 and **EBCDIC** (cp037, cp500, cp273, cp1140, cp1141, cp1047, cp875).

- The **source encoding is detected automatically** and preselected.
- The **preview** shows the source using the chosen codec.
- **Error strategy**: strict (report), replace or ignore.
- Write to a new file or **overwrite the original**.
*Tools → GitHub-Alarm* meldet neue Pushe:
*Tools → GitHub alarm* reports new pushes.

- **Repository** as `owner/repo` or as a GitHub URL (also `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`).
- An optional **token** raises the API limit and is stored in the keychain, not in plain text.
- The timestamp of the last push is checked; if it changes you get a notification. *Check now* queries immediately.
*Tools → Makro-Manager* bietet ein Raste:
*Tools → Macro manager* provides a grid of freely assignable keys.

- **Layers** (pages) on the left: create, edit (name, associated application, rows × columns), delete. Import/export as JSON.
- **Edit mode**: clicking a key opens the editor. **Run mode**: clicking triggers the action, press and hold still opens the editor.
- *Switch layer automatically to match the application* watches the foreground application and switches accordingly.

In the **key editor**: label and its position, icon (as background), font colour/family and the **action**. Depending on the action type the matching payload editor appears — text, number, layer, window, SSH command, JSON or a **sequence** of several steps.

Actions include launching programs, simulating keyboard/mouse, managing windows, controlling media, HTTP requests and sending commands to the consoles.
*Tools → Netzwerk-Scanner* durchsucht da:

- Options: ping, reachable only, resolve names, shares, detect services.

**Shortcuts** — every action is freely assignable; **duplicates are reported** when saving. *Reset to defaults* restores the presets.

Language and font sizes take effect after a restart.
`Strg+Alt+F` durchsucht Datei-**Inhalte*:
`Ctrl+Alt+F` searches file **contents**.

- **Search term** literal or as a **regex**.
- **Whole word** restricts to word boundaries.
- **Binary files** are skipped by default.
- **Context** shows N lines before and after the hit.
- Result lines have the form `path:line:text`; double-click opens the file's folder.
`Strg+P` öffnet den **Befehlskatalog** —:
`Ctrl+P` opens the **command catalogue** — sortable by command, category, platform and description.

- **OS filter**: Current OS · All · Linux only · Windows only · Cross-platform. The server OS is detected on connect.
- **Dangerous commands** are marked in red.
- **Assistant…** opens the parameter editor: text fields, dropdowns and checkboxes with a **live preview**. On Linux additionally **sudo** (optionally as another user).
- *Insert* writes the command into the console, *Run* executes it.
`Strg+Shift+F` sucht nach Dateinamen.\n\:
`Ctrl+Shift+F` searches for file names.

- **Pattern**: wildcards (`*.log`) or **regex**.
- **Only files (globs)** and **exclude folders** (each comma-separated).
- **Ignore case** is preset.
- Hits arrive live; **Stop** aborts.
- Double-clicking a hit navigates to its folder.
`Strg+Shift+R` benennt die markierten Da:
`Ctrl+Shift+R` renames the selected files in one go.

**Search & replace** — mode *Text* (literal), *Wildcards* (`*`/`?`) or *Regex*; optionally ignore case.

**Text & extension** — prefix, suffix, letter case (lower/UPPER/Title/Sentence), spaces (keep/`_`/`-`/remove) and extension (unchanged/lower/UPPER/set).

**Numbering** — start, step, digits, separator, position (start/end) as well as the **order** for assigning numbers (input, name, natural `1,2,10`, extension).

The **preview** shows old → new; changed names are green, conflicts red. *Number conflicts automatically* appends ` (1)`, ` (2)` … Execution follows a **safe order** — swaps (`a↔b`) and chains (`a→b→c`) work via temporary intermediate names.
`Strg+Shift+T` öffnet Port-Weiterleitung:
`Ctrl+Shift+T` opens port forwardings (the tab must be connected):

- **Local (-L)**: a local port is forwarded to a target behind the server — e.g. `127.0.0.1:8080` → `localhost:80` on the server.
- **Remote (-R)**: a port on the server points to a local target.
- **Dynamic (-D)**: SOCKS5 proxy over the SSH connection.

Open tunnels are listed and can be **stopped** individually; they are closed automatically when the tab is closed.
